study.title: Increased low frequency fluctuation in the brain after acupuncture treatment in CSVDCI patients: A randomized control trial study
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial using fMRI scans to assess the effect and mechanisms of acupuncture treatment on CSVDCI
study.randomization: A random number generator with SPSS 22.0 statistical software was used by a researcher specializing in random assignment to derive 60 random numbers and generate a random assignment sequence. The cards with the random numbers, groupings, and interventions were then concealed in airtight, opaque envelopes.
study.blinding: The researcher responsible for randomization was not allowed to participate in the recruitment screening, outcome assessment and statistical analysis. Cognitive assessors were blinded to group assignment (implied by separate personnel). Full participant/assessor blinding details not fully reported.
study.population: CSVDCI patients recruited at the neurology outpatient and inpatient departments of Zhongshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine
study.disease_condition: Cerebral small vessel disease cognitive impairment (CSVDCI)
study.inclusion_criteria: (i) age between 40 and 80 years, (ii) comply with diagnostic imaging criteria for cerebral small vessel disease and vascular cognitive impairment, (iii) MoCA score between 10 and 26, (iv) not receiving regular acupuncture treatment for the recent six months
study.exclusion_criteria: (i) cognitive dysfunction caused by macrovascular, cardiogenic cerebral embolism, (ii) patients with severe speech, vision, or hearing impairments or mental disorders that impact cognitive examinations, (iii) cognitive dysfunction caused by neuropsychological disorders (e.g., depression), (iv) illiterates that could not cooperate with cognitive examinations, (v) prior alcohol and drug abuse experience, (vi) combination of serious diseases, including of the cardiovascular, hepatic, nephrology, endocrine system and hematopoietic systems, (vii) participating in other clinical trials

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Acupuncture at Shenting and Baihui acupoints combined with conventional treatment
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Shenting: on the head, 0.5 inch straight up from the middle of the front hairline. Baihui: located at the intersection of the median line at the top of the head and the line connecting the tips of the two ears.
interventions.manipulation_exact: With the thumb and forefinger holding the needle handle, the doctor alternately twists the needle body clockwise and counterclockwise to make it rotate quickly (180–300 times/min), and continues twisting for 2–3 min. After this, twist once every 10 min (following Deqi), and keep the needle for 40 min.
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once a day, for five days a week over a total of 12 weeks
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: Yang Xiaoyan, an associate chief physician who practices acupuncture for more than 10 years
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Various ancient and modern acupuncture publications showed the Shenting (GV24) and Baihui (GV20) are vital distal acupoints associated with the cure of dementia, dizziness, headache, among other brain diseases.

Conventional treatment included donepezil tablets to improve cognition, aspirin to anti-platelet aggregation, atorvastatin calcium tablets to regulate lipid levels, in addition to blood pressure and blood glucose control according to the patient's underlying disease, and each patient participated in modern cognitive rehabilitation training.

sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: Deqi was intended; manipulation was continued following Deqi (twist once every 10 min following Deqi)
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi is mentioned as a procedural marker for acupuncture technique but not formally assessed or quantified as an outcome measure in this study.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: GE 3T MRI scanner with an 8-channel phased-array head coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: gradient echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence; high resolution brain structural images acquired using a T1-weighed 3D BRAVO sequence
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: 3 mm3 × 3 mm3 × 3 mm3 (normalized functional); slice thickness = 3.5 mm, inter-slice gap = 0.7 mm (functional acquisition); slice thickness = 1 mm (structural)
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: PALM implemented in the DPARSF toolbox; DPABI package; SPSS version 22.0
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel of 5 mm full width at half maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: head motion displacement > 3 mm or rotation > 3° in any axis (x, y, and z-axis)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: temporal band-pass filtering for the typical band (0.01–0.08 Hz)
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: not_reported; WM and CSF signals were regressed
statistical_thresholds_exact: corrected two-tailed P value < 0.05, cluster size > 200 voxels (within-group paired t-test with TFCE and FWE correction)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Permutation tests and multiple comparison corrections applied to all statistics; threshold free cluster enhancement (TFCE) and family wise error (FWE) methods with the DPABI package (for within-group paired t-test); no correction for between-group ALFF comparison

extraction_notes.note: Expectancy, treatment credibility, and blinding success were not formally assessed or reported in this study. No expectancy instrument was administered to participants.
Adverse events were not reported in the paper. There is no mention of any adverse events section or statement that no adverse events occurred.

The paper does not include a sham acupuncture arm. The control group received conventional treatment only (pharmacological and cognitive rehabilitation). There is no placebo or sham needling comparison.

The statistical threshold for the between-group ALFF comparison (Table 4) is stated as P < 0.005 with no correction. The within-group paired t-test (Table 5) uses corrected P < 0.05 with TFCE and FWE. These different thresholds should be interpreted cautiously in any meta-analysis.

The paper refers to 'left superior occipital gyrus' in the results and abstract (P = 0.011, correlated with MoCA), but the conclusion section states 'left inferior occipital gyrus.' This is an internal inconsistency in the paper. The coordinate table shows 'Occipital_Mid/Sup_L' at MNI -33, -72, 15 which covers both middle and superior occipital regions.

The conclusion section states 'left superior parietal gyrus' but the results section and Table 4 report 'right superior parietal gyrus' (Parietal_Sup_R, MNI 27, -51, 54). The correlation figure also labels this as 'Parietal_Sup_R'. The conclusion text appears to contain an error.

Table 3 reports 'Rank' as a column header for the pre-to-post differences, described as M(IQR). The column label 'Rank' is unusual and may reflect a Mann-Whitney U rank-based summary. The exact meaning of this column header is ambiguous and has been preserved as reported.

The paper states SDMT, VFT, BNT, DST with normal distribution were analyzed using independent t-test (Section 2.9.1), but Table 3 reports all five outcomes including DST and BNT using Mann-Whitney U test. This is an internal inconsistency regarding statistical tests used for between-group change comparisons.

The 'Occipital_Mid/Sup_L' entry in Table 4 (cluster size 81, MNI -33, -72, 15) corresponds to the abstract descriptions of both 'left middle occipital gyrus' and 'left superior occipital gyrus' as separate regions. The table appears to combine these into one cluster. In the correlation analysis (Figure 4 and Section 3.3), these are treated as separate ROIs. This may reflect extraction of two separate peaks from the same cluster or a discrepancy in reporting.

The paper does not report post-treatment absolute cognitive scores, only pre-to-post difference ranks and percentages. Absolute post-treatment values for MoCA, SDMT, VFT, DST, and BNT are not provided.
Deqi sensations were noted as a procedural criterion for needle manipulation but were not formally measured or quantified using a validated instrument (e.g., MASS, SAS). No deqi scores are reported.

The figure caption for Figure 2 labels regions as: a=right inferior temporal gyrus, b=right precuneus, c=left postcentral gyrus, d=left precentral gyrus, e=right postcentral gyrus, f=right superior parietal gyrus, g=left middle occipital gyrus, h=left insula, i=right cerebellum. The label 'd=left precentral gyrus' is listed in the figure caption but the corresponding atlas entry in Table 4 shows 'Precentral_R' (right). This is a discrepancy between the figure caption and the table.

The paper does not report correlation analyses between ALFF changes and MoCA for all regions in Table 4 (e.g., left insula, bilateral postcentral gyrus, right cerebellum, right precuneus, right precentral gyrus). Only four regions are reported in Figure 4 and Section 3.3.

Sample size calculation was based on MoCA differences reported in Wang et al. 2016. The effect value used was 1.194045, alpha=0.01, Power=0.9, yielding 23 cases per group, 56 total with 20% attrition, rounded to 28 per group (60 total enrolled).
